 29 Dhaka South wards at high risk of dengue, survey finds
 Aedes mosquito larvae and pupae found in 403 of 2,250 households surveyed 
 Published : 4 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 4 November 2026, 16:36
 • 
 DISEASE
 SHARE 
 Star Online Report 
 Twenty-nine of the 75 wards under Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) have been identified as high-risk areas for dengue transmission, while 28 are at moderate risk and 18 at low risk, according to a survey.
 DSCC Administrator Abdus Salam unveiled the findings at an event at Nagar Bhaban Auditorium in Dhaka this afternoon.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 A total of 36 DSCC field workers collected data from September 27 to October 8, surveying 2,250 households, with 30 selected from each ward.
 Presenting the findings, DSCC Chief Health Officer Dr Jahane Ferdous Binte Rahman said Aedes mosquito larvae and pupae were found in 403 households.
 Of the breeding sites identified, 31.6 percent were in multi-storey buildings, 31.37 percent in standalone houses, 17.39 percent in semi-pucca houses and 13.4 percent in buildings under construction. Vacant plots were also identified as breeding sites.
 Stagnant water on floors accounted for 12.26 percent of breeding sources, while water stored in buckets accounted for 10.34 percent.
 Speaking at the event, Abdus Salam urged residents to keep their homes and workplaces clean and remove stagnant water at least once a week, saying government initiatives alone would not be enough to prevent dengue.
